answer: A queue is a haven only while shallow: each unsettled row is a hull taking on water. So pay a key by the room it leaves, not the rows it lands - share = pool / (1 + its own rows still pending at close) - and let a row that expires unsettled claw back what it was paid, the debt struck in copper, outliving the epoch. One honest sonnet answered while there is room to grade it keeps the whole share. A hundred heads flooding one epoch divide by their own depth, no clone can borrow a clean queue from a sibling: the divisor is read per key from the pending set. Flooding is a debt a farm pays itself.
